title: Reduce hot-path copies and add session range indexes
body:
## Summary

Reduces hot-path copying, syscall overhead, and session range-query costs in psi:

- adds native session token prefix sums for O(1) tail token totals and O(log n) keep-recent range queries
- computes pi-style semantic token estimates in Lua, then stores the calibrated per-message estimate in C for fast range math
- applies the empirically calibrated formula `ceil(pi_tokens * 1.105)` to target roughly a 5% average overestimate on live OpenRouter chats
- adds a native JSONL append path for structured session entries, with Lua fallback for legacy/synthetic records
- buffers `read_file_slice` reads instead of using byte-at-a-time `fgetc`
- accumulates provider stream deltas in parts arrays before final concat
- removes JSON encode/decode boundaries in TUI layout/status paths and renders only the visible transcript window
- extends `tests/bench.py` with targeted benches and configurable per-run timeout for slow remote targets

I intentionally left the `ls` tool on the original path. A typed/native listing experiment regressed on hippocampus, so it was not kept in the tool path.

## Data Structures

Before this PR, the session was only a growable C array of `{role, text, data_json}` messages. Any range query crossed the C/Lua boundary by materializing Lua tables with `psi.session_messages()` or `psi.session_messages_from()`, then walking those tables in Lua. Context accounting and keep-recent selection were therefore O(n) scans over allocated Lua records, and append-only saves still decoded and re-encoded each new message through Lua's disk-entry formatter.

After this PR, each `psi_message` stores a token estimate supplied at append time, and `psi_session` maintains a parallel prefix-sum array where `token_prefix[i]` is the cumulative token estimate through message `i`. That keeps the transcript itself cache-friendly as flat arrays while adding compact range metadata. Tail context totals become one subtraction, `prefix[count] - prefix[start - 1]`, and keep-recent selection binary-searches the prefix array instead of reverse-scanning Lua message tables.

The schema-aware estimator lives in Lua, where the pi session/message shape is already being constructed and loaded. It mirrors pi's semantic approach: user text counts as text, assistant entries count text/thinking/tool-call names and arguments, tool results include text plus a fixed image charge, bash execution counts command and output, and compaction/branch summaries count summary text. C no longer parses pi JSON for this; its fallback for primitive callers is just calibrated chars/4 text.

The stored value is calibrated with `ceil(pi_tokens * 1.105)`, based on 54 live OpenRouter chat probes across Claude, Gemini, and GPT prompt sizes from short chats up to tens of thousands of characters. The total sample mean was about 1.05x real prompt tokens; individual provider/tokenizer cases can still undercount or overcount more than that.

The new native APIs are still policy-neutral: Lua decides when to compact, how to save, and how to interpret session schema, while C owns only the hot-path storage/index operations. The JSONL append fast path mirrors the existing disk-entry shape in C for structured records and falls back to the old Lua serializer if it sees a legacy/synthetic message without structured data.

## Benchmarks

Lower is better. Percentage is elapsed-time reduction.

### Initial Hot-Path Audit

Local x86_64 dynamic build:

| Bench | Before | After | Improvement | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `session_save_growing` | 2.7 ms | 1.6 ms | 40.7% | 1.7x |
| `session_turn_shape` | 3.2 ms | 1.3 ms | 59.4% | 2.5x |
| `session_append_delta` | 31.4 ms | 2.4 ms | 92.4% | 13.1x |
| `read_file_slice_large` | 531.2 ms | 133.9 ms | 74.8% | 4.0x |

hippocampus i686 static Linux:

| Bench | Before | After | Improvement | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `session_save_growing` | 121.3 ms | 50.1 ms | 58.7% | 2.4x |
| `session_turn_shape` | 123.0 ms | 47.5 ms | 61.4% | 2.6x |
| `session_append_delta` | 1534.4 ms | 82.6 ms | 94.6% | 18.6x |
| `read_file_slice_large` | 5110.4 ms | 1778.4 ms | 65.2% | 2.9x |

### Session Range Index Follow-Up

Local x86_64 dynamic build, baseline is the prior PR head before the range-index commit:

| Bench | Before | After | Improvement | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `context_range_queries` | 243.703 ms | 0.039 ms | 99.98% | 6248.8x |

hippocampus i686 static Linux, serial before/after runs from fresh copied binaries:

| Bench | Before | After | Improvement | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `context_range_queries` | 8405.476 ms | 2.472 ms | 99.97% | 3400.3x |
| `session_append_delta` | 83.7 ms | 58.6 ms | 30.0% | 1.4x |
| `session_turn_shape` | 47.0 ms | 39.1 ms | 16.8% | 1.2x |

## Token Calibration Check

A live-only one-off calibration run used 54 OpenRouter chat calls: Claude, Gemini, and GPT models; 9 randomized prompt sizes; 2 repeats. The fitted lines compare estimate against provider-reported prompt tokens.

| Group | Old R² | Old fit | New R² | New fit |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Total | 0.989176 | `y=0.891205x+135.77` | 0.989176 | `y=0.984793x+150.24` |
| Claude | 0.997298 | `y=0.878078x+99.41` | 0.997297 | `y=0.970287x+110.05` |
| Gemini | 0.997371 | `y=0.839247x+94.35` | 0.997371 | `y=0.927379x+104.47` |
| GPT-5.4 | 0.995742 | `y=0.990188x+93.41` | 0.995742 | `y=1.094171x+103.43` |

Across the total sample, old estimate mean ratio was 0.951x real tokens; new estimate mean ratio is 1.051x real tokens.

title: Build: tolerate older gcc and Lua's long long lua_Integer
body:
## Summary

Two small portability fixes uncovered by building `psi` on Alpine Linux 3.14 (gcc 10.3.1, system Lua 5.4) without the nix flake.

- **Makefile**: add `-Wno-long-long` to `STRICT_CFLAGS`. Lua 5.4's `luaconf.h` unconditionally types `lua_Integer` as `long long`, which trips `-std=c89 -pedantic` in any TU that includes `lua.h`. We keep `-std=c89` for our own translation units and only suppress this single warning, which is forced on us by the embedded Lua headers.
- **src/core/process.c**: only emit the `-Wanalyzer-fd-leak` diagnostic pragma on gcc ≥ 13. The flag was [added in gcc 13](https://gcc.gnu.org/gcc-13/changes.html); older gccs (e.g. Alpine 3.14's 10.3.1) reject the unknown pragma under `-Werror=pragmas`. `clang` and `tinycc` were already excluded.

No behavioral change on toolchains where `-fanalyzer` is available; the `__GNUC__ >= 13` gate just makes the suppression a no-op on older gcc instead of a hard error.

## Verification

On Alpine 3.14 / gcc 10.3.1 with default flags (no env overrides):

```
make clean && make
build/psi --version   # -> 0.1.0
```

(Also requires `argtable3` available to the linker; that part is environment-specific and not changed here.)

title: Add Codex provider (OpenAI Responses API)
body:
## Summary

Adds a fourth wired provider, **Codex**, that talks the OpenAI **Responses API** (`POST /v1/responses` with SSE streaming) — the wire format the [`codex` CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) speaks. Selectable via:

```bash
psi --model=codex/gpt-5.1-codex
psi --model=codex/gpt-5.5
PSI_PROVIDER=codex psi
```

## Why a self-contained provider (not `openai_compat`)

The Responses API is structurally different from chat/completions:

| | chat/completions | Responses |
|---|---|---|
| messages | `messages: [{role, content}]` | `input: [items]` (typed) |
| tools | `[{type:"function", function:{...}}]` | `[{type:"function", name, ...}]` (flat) |
| system | `{role:"system", content}` | top-level `instructions` |
| max output | `max_tokens` | `max_output_tokens` |
| tool calls | nested in assistant message | separate `function_call` items |
| tool results | `{role:"tool", tool_call_id, content}` | `function_call_output` items |
| reasoning | none / hidden | `reasoning.{effort,summary}` + dedicated SSE events |

So this provider owns its session→input transform, SSE parser, and request body builder rather than going through `psi.openai_compat`.

## Auth chain (priority order)

1. `OPENAI_API_KEY`
2. `CODEX_API_KEY` (alias)
3. `~/.codex/auth.json` — the codex CLI's stored ChatGPT login. Either the `OPENAI_API_KEY` field or the OAuth `tokens.access_token` is picked up automatically, so this works out of the box on machines that have already run `codex login`.

## Env knobs

| Variable | Effect |
|---|---|
| `PSI_CODEX_MODEL` | Default model when none is passed (default `gpt-5.1-codex`) |
| `PSI_CODEX_BASE_URL` | Override `https://api.openai.com/` (proxies / Azure) |
| `PSI_CODEX_REASONING_EFFORT` | `minimal` \| `low` \| `medium` \| `high` → `reasoning.effort` |
| `PSI_CODEX_REASONING_SUMMARY` | `auto` \| `concise` \| `detailed` \| `none` → `reasoning.summary` |

`store: false` and `parallel_tool_calls: true` are sent on every request so psi owns history and tool calls fan out cooperatively (matching pi's behaviour).

## SSE events handled

- `response.created` — captures server-side response_id
- `response.output_text.delta` — assistant text streaming
- `response.reasoning_summary_text.delta` / `response.reasoning_text.delta` — reasoning streams (mapped to psi's existing `thinking-delta` event)
- `response.output_item.added` — function_call announcement (id, call_id, name)
- `response.function_call_arguments.{delta,done}` — accumulated tool-call arguments
- `response.completed` — usage totals (with cache_read disambiguation matching `openai_compat`)
- `response.failed` / `response.error` — error envelope

Cross-provider session replay drops thinking blocks (Responses-API reasoning items are tied to a server-side response_id and cannot be reused across requests).

## Tests

5 new tests, all passing locally:

| Test | What it covers |
|---|---|
| `providers/codex_routing` | Registry wiring: `codex/gpt-5.1-codex` → codex provider → `openai-responses` API → `psi.codex` module |
| `codex/sse_parser` | Byte-by-byte SSE feed reconstructs text deltas, function_call arguments, and usage totals (catches chunk-boundary regressions) |
| `codex/build_api_input` | Session→Responses-input transform: `input_text` / `output_text` content, separate `function_call` and `function_call_output` items, orphan tool_result drop |
| `codex/request_body_shape` | Verifies `input` not `messages`, `instructions` not `system`, `max_output_tokens` not `max_tokens`, `store:false`, `stream:true`, `parallel_tool_calls:true` |
| `codex/finalize_malformed_args` | Truncated function_call arguments JSON falls back to `{}` with a stderr warning rather than crashing |

The existing `providers/api_registry` test was bumped from 3 → 4 APIs to reflect the new `openai-responses` entry.

title: Detach child stdin so ESC interrupts long tool calls
body:
## Summary

Pressing ESC during a long-running tool call (e.g. `find /`, `make build`) had no effect — the turn could not be interrupted. Root cause: the spawned child inherits the parent's stdin = the TUI's controlling terminal in raw/no-echo mode, so keypresses raced between the child and ncurses.

## Fix

Redirect the child's stdin to `/dev/null` in `psi_process_begin_exec` (a single `dup2`). All key bytes now reach ncurses; `psi.abort_trigger` fires; the in-flight tool's child gets SIGTERM via the existing abort path.

## Side benefit

Tools that read stdin (`cat`, `sort`, etc. with no argument) used to block forever waiting for input from a fd no one feeds. They now see immediate EOF and exit cleanly.

## Verification

```lua
-- Before: total_ticks was 0 from sched.run_all in eval mode (no host hook).
```

title: tools: port pi-mono's truncate.ts and bash spillover
body:
## What

Ports pi-mono's tool-output truncation (`packages/coding-agent/src/core/tools/truncate.ts`) into psi. Before this PR, every spawned process was hard-capped at 256 KiB inside `src/core/process.c`: any bytes past that point were dropped on the floor and only a `truncated=true` boolean was returned to the model. Long bash logs lost their tails (where errors live), `grep` on a minified file could blow the byte budget on a single line, and the model was never told what it was missing or where to look for the rest.

## How

### `lua/psi/truncate.lua`

Mirrors `truncateHead` / `truncateTail` / `truncateLine` / `formatSize` from pi:

- defaults: **2000 lines / 50 KiB / 500 chars per long line**
- `truncate_head` (read/grep/ls/find): keeps first N, never returns partial lines, special-cases "first line alone exceeds byte limit"
- `truncate_tail` (bash): keeps last N; if a single trailing line exceeds the byte cap, slices it on a UTF-8 boundary and flags `last_line_partial=true`
- `truncate_line` clips a single line to N chars and adds `... [truncated]`
- `head_notice` / `tail_notice` build the `[Showing lines X-Y of Z. Full output: /tmp/...]` strings so the model knows where to read more

Old `by_lines` / `bytes` / `notice` helpers stay (still used by `read.lua`).

### `lua/psi/tool_shell.lua`

New `run_streaming{,_argv}` driver:

- drives `psi.process_begin / poll / finish` from Lua
- accumulates a rolling in-memory buffer (~4× max bytes) so tail-truncation has data to work with
- once total bytes exceed the soft cap, opens a temp file and appends every chunk so the **full** output is preserved on disk
- works inside a TUI coroutine (yields via `sched.proc_poll`) and outside one (blocks via `psi.process_poll`); same code path either way

### Tool wiring

| tool | behaviour |
|---|---|
| **bash** | tail-truncates; if truncated, surfaces `extras.temp_file_path` and appends `[Showing lines X-Y of Z. Full output: /tmp/...]` so the model can `read` the rest |
| **grep** | head-truncates **and** clips individual match lines to 500 chars |
| **find** | head-truncates by bytes (line cap delegated to `fd --max-results`) |
| **ls** | existing entry cap kept; byte cap layered on top |
| **read** | unchanged (offset/limit paging is already pi-shaped) |

### New host primitives in `src/lua/vm.c`

- `psi.file_append(path, content)` — `fopen("ab")` + `fwrite`. Used by the bash spillover.
- `psi.tempfile_path([prefix])` — picks `$TMPDIR/$prefix-<pid>-<ts>-<counter>` without creating the file. C89-clean, no `mkstemp` dependency.

Both are advertised in `runtime_info` and documented in `docs/extensions.md`.

### Tool description strings

Every output-producing tool now advertises its limits and the temp-file hint in its description, so the model can plan around them — matches pi's tool-card style.

## Tests

Nine new smoke tests in `tests/smoke.py`:

- `truncate/format_size`
- `truncate/head_lines` / `head_bytes` / `head_first_line_too_big`
- `truncate/tail_lines` / `tail_partial_last_line`
- `truncate/line_clip`
- `tool/bash_truncates_long_output` (200 KB → tail-truncated + temp-file hint in output)
- `tool/bash_short_output_no_truncation`
- `tool/bash_writes_temp_file_when_truncated` (reads the spillover file back to confirm it has the full payload)
- `tool/grep_clips_long_lines`

```
$ ./tests/smoke.py --no-live
81 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped  (51.0s)
```

## Notes

- The 256 KiB cap inside `src/core/process.c` stays as a final backstop but is no longer load-bearing — the soft 50 KiB cap is enforced in Lua with proper head/tail semantics, and the temp file holds whatever wouldn't fit inline.
- Behaviour-preserving for the existing `process_result{,_argv}` / `run_tool{,_argv}` helpers; only the five wired-up tools opt into the new streaming path.

title: tui: redirect stderr to a log file while curses owns the screen
body:
## Summary

Fix sticky stderr text on the TUI input prompt when a turn hits a transient HTTP error (e.g. `anthropic: http transport error`).

## Bug

When `provider_loop.lua` fails a request (curl returns -1), it writes the failure message to `stderr` before returning to the caller:

https://github.com/siraben/psi-code/blob/master/lua/psi/provider_loop.lua#L189

In `--tui` mode that file descriptor is the live terminal. ncurses didn't write those bytes itself, so its internal line cache treats the affected row as unchanged and never repaints over it. The message ends up glued to whatever curses last drew there — usually the input prompt row — until the user types enough characters to push the row out of the visible area.

Reproduction (no real API key needed):

```bash
PSI_ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://no-such-host.invalid/ \
  ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=fake ./build/psi --tui
# type "hello" and press Enter
```

Before the fix, the prompt row reads:

```
> anthropic: http transport error          1  ctx:0.0% ...
```

The same hazard exists for every other `io.stderr:write(...)` and `fprintf(stderr, ...)` site (sched tick errors, anthropic teardown, openai_compat HTTP errors, events handler failures, vm bootstrap errors, etc.) — anything that fires while curses owns the screen.

## Fix

Redirect fd 2 to a log file for the duration of the TUI session, in `src/runtime/tui_mode.c`:

- Before `initscr()`: `dup()` the original stderr, open `$XDG_STATE_HOME/psi/tui-stderr.log` (fall back to `$HOME/.local/state/psi/tui-stderr.log`), `dup2()` it onto `STDERR_FILENO`.
- After `endwin()`: `dup2()` the saved fd back so post-shutdown error messages (e.g. `psi.modes.run error: ...`) reach the user's terminal as before.

This catches every stderr writer — both Lua-side `io.stderr:write` and C-side `fprintf(stderr, ...)` — without touching call sites.

The TUI runtime already routes provider failures through `add_entry("error", ...)` + `set_status(..., true)` (see `tui_runtime.lua:1062-1075`), so the user-visible error reporting path is unchanged. What was extra was the duplicate, screen-corrupting stderr write.

After the fix, the same reproduction shows a clean prompt row and a normal `agent turn failed` status; the actual error text is in `~/.local/state/psi/tui-stderr.log` for diagnostics.

## Validation

Tested on Alpine 3.11.2 i686 (iSH on iOS), gcc 10.3.1 and tcc 0.9.28rc:

```bash
make -j4
make -j4 CC=tcc HOST_CC=cc STRICT_CFLAGS="" \
    RPATH_LDFLAGS='$(LOCAL_RPATH_LDFLAGS)'
./tests/smoke.py --no-live   # 70 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped
```

Reproduced the bug under tmux on `master`, then verified the same flow under the patched build:

| Run                             | Prompt row after the failed turn          | Log file |
| ---                             | ---                                       | --- |
| master                          | `> anthropic: http transport error  1 ...` (sticky) | n/a |
| `ben/tui-stderr-redirect`       | `>` (clean)                                | `anthropic: http transport error\n` |

## Notes

- `O_TRUNC` on the log: a fresh log per TUI session keeps it small and scannable. Switching to `O_APPEND` would be reasonable if anyone wants cross-session history; happy to flip if you'd prefer.
- All `mkdir`/`open`/`dup2` failures degrade silently — if the redirect fails for any reason the TUI launches with original stderr (the pre-fix behavior). Better than failing the launch outright.
- No changes to `provider_loop.lua` or any other Lua module. The host-side fix is the right layer because the corruption is fundamentally about fd 2 going to the wrong place during curses, not about any single error message.

title: Codebase-review fixes, pi-mono renames, Makefile refactor
body:
Three layers of work, one commit each (rebased on `origin/master`):

## 1. Codebase-review fixes + pi-mono renames

Applies 14 fixes (1 blocking, 12 should-fix, 1 nit) surfaced by a Claude+Codex review of the working tree, plus file renames so names match content and (where pi-mono is authoritative) match pi-mono's spelling.

### Blocking
- **OAuth token chmod race** (`lua/psi/auth_storage.lua` + new `psi.file_write_secure`): credentials hit disk via `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|0600` + `fsync` + `rename` + parent dirsync. Eliminates both the brief-`0644` window and the failed-chmod-leaves-leaked-tokens path.

### Should-fix
- **Abort signals process group** (`src/core/process.c`): `setpgid` in child + parent, `kill(-pgid, ...)`, SIGKILL escalation after 500ms. SIGTERM-ignoring grandchildren no longer hang abort.
- **Session JSONL durability** (`src/lua/vm.c` + `lua/psi/session_manager.lua`): single `fwrite` per record + `fflush`+`fsync`; atomic temp+rename for full saves via new `psi.file_write_atomic`.
- **Truncated tool args** (`lua/psi/providers/{anthropic,openrouter,openai_codex}.lua`): record `state.malformed_tool_input_error`, surface via `stream_error` so the turn fails instead of dispatching with `{}`.
- **libcurl global-cleanup race** (`src/core/{http_async,http_buffered}.c`): per-call init/cleanup replaced with `pthread_once`-guarded `psi_http_global_init`.
- **`curl_slist_append` leak** (same files): new `psi_http_slist_append_safe` frees prior list and aborts on NULL return.
- **`runtime_info().primitives` stale** (`src/lua/vm.c`): now derived at call time by walking the live `psi` table.
- **`psi_vm_argv_from_table` leak** (`src/lua/vm.c`): pre-validate types, then `lua_tostring` + NULL-handle; previous `luaL_checkstring` would `longjmp` past cleanup.
- **C owned session disk schema** (`src/lua/vm.c`): drop `psi_vm_session_disk_entry` + `lfn_session_append_jsonl`. Schema lives in `lua/psi/session_manager.lua`'s `to_disk_entry`; C host no longer carries session semantics.
- **`grep`/`find` flag-leak** (`lua/psi/tools/{grep,find}.lua`): `--` separator inserted so flag-shaped patterns match literally.

### Nit
- **`openai_codex` dead branch**: export `anthropic.maybe_auto_compact` and use it; previous `_maybe_auto_compact` lookup was never exported.

### Renames (file/path layer; public namespace stays short)
- C: `src/core/anthropic.{c,h}` → `http_buffered.{c,h}`; `src/runtime/print_mode.c` → `cli_mode.c`; `src/core/agent.c` → `agent_runtime.c`; `scripts/embed_lua.c` → `embed.c`.
- Lua, mirroring pi-mono's `-manager`/`-bus`/`-loader`/`-session` suffixes: `session.lua` → `session_manager.lua`, `settings.lua` → `settings_manager.lua`, `events.lua` → `event_bus.lua`, `commands.lua` → `slash_commands.lua`, `resources.lua` → `resource_loader.lua`, `agent.lua` → `agent_session.lua`, `message_transform.lua` → `transform_messages.lua`, `tool_mutation_queue.lua` → `file_mutation_queue.lua`, `path.lua` → `path_utils.lua`, `json.lua` → `json_pure.lua`, `providers.lua` → `api_registry.lua`, `tui.lua` → `tui_status.lua`.
- Move all 7 provider files into `lua/psi/providers/`, mirroring pi-mono's `packages/ai/src/providers/` split.
- Add 1-line docstrings to every `lua/psi/tools/*.lua` and to `lua/psi/theme.lua` so the existing convention holds across all Lua files.

## 2. Makefile refactor (3 commits)

- **Per-object duplication → pattern rule.** 12 hand-maintained per-`.o` rules collapse to one static pattern over `$(OBJECTS)`. Source list auto-discovered with `find src -name '*.c'`. Header dependencies auto-generated via `-MMD -MP` and pulled in with `-include`. pkg-config dependency block uses a single `PKG_DEPS = "VAR:pkg …"` list with `$(foreach)` over `$(call dep_cflags,…)`/`$(call dep_libs,…)`.
- **Static pattern rules + idiom upgrades.** `$(OBJECTS): $(BUILD_DIR)/%.o: %.c` binds the recipe to a specific target list. `firstword`/`lastword` replace `$(word 1,…)`/`$(word 2,…)`. `check-curl-ca` becomes order-only so its `.PHONY` status no longer relinks every build. `.DEFAULT_GOAL := all` makes default-target intent explicit.
- **Portable opt-out for auto-deps.** `-MMD -MP` lifted into `DEPFLAGS`; `make DEPFLAGS=` disables header-driven rebuild tracking on toolchains that can't emit gcc-style `.d` files (Plan 9 pcc, sas/c). Build itself is unaffected.

Net Makefile change: ~263 → ~228 lines, with comments trimmed to load-bearing rationale only.

## Rejected during cross-validation (in chain-of-thought)
- `psi_http_post/get` response-body NULL on OOM — caller normalizes NULL to `""`.
- `lfn_tool_call` shadowed by `boot.lua` — pure cleanup, no runtime failure.
- Path-escape via `..` in write/edit tools — out-of-scope per `docs/port-status.md` ("no sandboxing").
- Header-strdup NULL not checked — speculative OOM path; `curl_slist_append` tolerates NULL strings.

title: Add dual-model PR review skill
body:
Adds `.claude/skills/dual-pr-review/SKILL.md` — a Claude+Codex review skill layered on top of the existing `.codex/skills/psi-pr-review` review lens.

## Pipeline

- **Phase 0** — gather diff against `origin/master`, walk per-file `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` scope, load per-area docs only when relevant (portability for C, port-status for parity, providers for provider changes, …).
- **Phase 1** — one summary pass to establish author intent, changed areas, high-risk areas, and per-pass focus.
- **Phase 2** — parallel discovery:
  - Codex A: architecture & instruction compliance (quote exact rules).
  - Codex B: adversarial bug hunt (trust boundaries, irreversible state, retry/concurrency, signal-safety, partial-write, command/path injection, libcurl/pthread races, abort propagation).
  - Claude opus per-area subagents: each gets a non-overlapping slice of the diff plus the psi review lens.
- **Phase 3** — cross-model validation: each model verifies the other's findings against the actual code; rejected findings move to chain-of-thought, not the final report.
- **Phase 4** — one markdown report at `reviews/PR-<N>.md`.

The skill enforces the same anti-hallucination gates and drop rules as the existing `psi-pr-review` skill: read the actual file, trace data flow, no "likely"/"probably", drop anything pre-existing or out-of-scope per `docs/port-status.md`.

## First-run validation

A first run of this skill against PR #47 lives on the `review/pr-47` branch (`reviews/PR-47.md`). It surfaced three should-fix findings in the new TUI markdown component:
1. Single-hyphen rows accepted as GFM table separators (`tui_components/markdown.lua:174`).
2. Double-backtick code spans break table-row parsing (`tui_components/markdown.lua:110-113`).
3. Theme switch leaves stale ANSI in the component + transcript caches (`tui_components/markdown.lua:523-541` and `tui_runtime.lua:667-668`).

Two Codex findings were rejected during Claude's validation pass (pre-existing patterns not worsened by the PR), confirming the cross-validation step does its job.

title: ESP32 firmware: live agent end-to-end via QEMU + C-native turn driver
body:
Targets `ben/capabilities`. Brings up psi as ESP32 firmware in QEMU
with a live Anthropic round-trip.

## End-to-end demo

```
$ source .env.local
$ nix run .#qemu              # boots ESP32 firmware in qemu-system-xtensa
psi web chat: http://localhost:8765
$ python -m websocket -> /ws -> {"type":"user","text":"Reply with PONG."}
   delta: 'PONG.'
   turn_end
```

## What landed

- **C-native agent path** (`src/backend/esp/esp_agent.c`): builds the
  Anthropic JSON request, streams the SSE response via `esp_http_client`,
  parses event/data lines inline, forwards `content_block_delta` text
  to the WebSocket observer. ~280 lines, no Lua state in the path.
  The Lua VM still loads at boot for future eval/tools work but the
  agent turn bypasses it entirely.
- **Embedded SPA** (`assets/web/index.html`): single-file vanilla-JS
  WebSocket chat. Streams assistant deltas into the DOM as they arrive.
- **HTTP+WS server** (`src/backend/esp/esp_ws_server.c`): `esp_http_server`
  with `/`, `/healthz`, and `/ws` routes; per-connection observer +
  outbox queue. Process-wide singleton VM (heap is too tight for
  per-connection state on ESP32).
- **Network bring-up** (`src/backend/esp/esp_main.c`): NVS init →
  read `anthropic_key` → `setenv ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` → Lua VM init
  before lwIP brings up its buffers → openeth Ethernet via slirp NAT
  → start HTTP server.
- **ESP-IDF project** (`firmware/`): CMake project, sdkconfig with
  PSRAM enabled, hardware crypto disabled (QEMU doesn't model it),
  `MBEDTLS_EXTERNAL_MEM_ALLOC=y` to route TLS buffers to PSRAM,
  unicore mode, 2 MiB factory partition, 30 s task watchdog.
- **psi as IDF component** (`components/psi/CMakeLists.txt`): globs
  the relevant psi C/Lua tree, runs `scripts/embed.c --no-compress`
  to bake Lua sources verbatim (no zlib at runtime), passes the
  capability gates from `ben/capabilities`.
- **Lua component** (`components/lua-cmod/`): vendors Lua 5.5 sources
  fetched from upstream tarball at flake-eval time.
- **Nix integration** (`flake.nix`):
  - `nixpkgs-esp-dev` overlay → `esp-idf-esp32` + `qemu-esp32`
  - `packages.firmware`: builds merged-flash 4 MiB image
  - `apps.qemu`: copies firmware to writable scratch, seeds NVS from
    `$ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, runs Espressif's QEMU fork with user-mode
    networking, `hostfwd=tcp::8765-:80`
  - `apps.flash`: real-hardware flash via esptool
  - `devShells.esp`: idf + qemu + python deps for ad-hoc work
- **Tests** (`tests/test_esp_qemu.py`, `tests/test_esp_live.py`):
  opt-in via `--run-firmware`; live test asserts a `PONG` round-trip
  through the C agent.

## Notes

- TLS works in QEMU only with the Espressif QEMU fork (`qemu-esp32`).
  Stock nixpkgs `qemu-system-xtensa` lacks the ESP32 peripheral models.
- mbedTLS hardware acceleration must be off; the official ESP-IDF
  `https_mbedtls` example does the same.
- The Lua agent loop crashed under PSRAM in QEMU (heap fragmentation
  + GC corruption on per-turn allocations). The C agent sidesteps it
  by never building a Lua-resident message history. Real-hardware
  may not need this, but the C path is simpler regardless.

## Verification

Desktop suite (153 smoke tests) still green. Live ESP suite gated on
`--run-firmware` and `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`:

```
$ pytest tests/test_esp_live.py --run-firmware
test_healthz PASSED
test_index_served PASSED
test_pong_round_trip PASSED
test_two_consecutive_turns PASSED
```

title: Capability gates, RAMFS, HTTP backend selector, slim boot
body:
Splits storage into explicit capability classes, gates fork/exec and
zlib-compressed embedding the same way, and adds an HTTP backend
selector — all groundwork for porting psi to ESP32 (PR follows on
`ben/esp32`), but each piece stands on its own and ships with the
desktop suite still green at 153/153.

## Commits

- **Capability gates and RAMFS storage backend** — adds
  `psi.runtime_info().capabilities` (`embedded_resources`, `ramfs`,
  `filesystem`, `process`, `http`, `tui`, `env`, `stdio`), wires the
  `PSI_CAP_*` macros that drive them, and adds a Lua-side RAMFS at
  `@mem/`. `@embedded/` becomes a first-class read-only namespace
  alongside the host filesystem. Tools / sessions / extensions consult
  the capability table instead of assuming POSIX.
- **Use slash-form embedded keys to match source layout** — embed.c
  was producing dotted keys (`psi.tools.read`) that didn't round-trip
  cleanly with the docs table or the SPA path. Now keys mirror the
  source path (`psi/tools/read.lua`); the C `require()` searcher
  translates Lua dotted names back at lookup time.
- **Gate process capability in C and Lua** — fork/exec primitives
  (`process_run`, `process_begin`, etc.) and `os.execute` / `io.popen`
  are now gated on `PSI_CAP_PROCESS`. Constrained builds (no shell)
  drop the entire `src/core/process.c` translation unit and refuse
  the Lua-side equivalents.
- **HTTP backend selector and slim boot module** — splits the libcurl
  HTTP layer behind `PSI_HTTP_BACKEND_CURL` so an alternate backend
  (esp_http_client / mbedTLS for ESP-IDF) can implement the same
  `psi_http.h` interface without touching desktop callers. Adds
  `lua/boot-esp.lua`, a slim bootstrap selected when
  `PSI_CAP_FILESYSTEM=0` so embedded targets get a smaller require
  graph.

## Verification

```
$ make && PSI_BIN=./build/psi pytest tests/smoke.py
153 passed, 6 skipped
```

Constrained build (`make CFLAGS="-DPSI_CAP_FILESYSTEM=0 -DPSI_CAP_PROCESS=0"`)
also builds clean and runs the slim boot.

title: Make TUI input and text helpers UTF-8 aware
body:
## Summary

The TUI editor, display-width math, byte-truncation helpers, and the pure-Lua JSON fallback all walked text byte-by-byte — anything non-ASCII (accented Latin, CJK, emoji, ZWJ sequences, JSON `\uD83D\uDE00`) got corrupted or silently dropped. This PR makes those surfaces codepoint-aware.

- **C input plumbing** — `psi_vm_tui_normalize_key` now assembles full UTF-8 sequences (1-4 bytes) from the lead byte before emitting a `text` event. Typing or pasting non-ASCII into the TUI used to drop bytes or stall on `isprint`; now it goes in cleanly.
- **Cell width via mk_wcwidth** — Markus Kuhn's public-domain wcwidth table lives in `src/core/wcwidth.c` (C89-clean, no allocation, no globals, no locale dependency) and is exposed as `psi.cell_width(cp)`. The Lua side queries it; no Unicode range tables in Lua. CJK / emoji / fullwidth report width 2; combining marks / format chars / variation selectors report 0.
- **TUI editor** — `state.cursor` arithmetic (move-left/right, delete-backward/forward, vim-append, the cursor cell render) now steps codepoints via `utf8.offset`. Input wrap (`build_input_lines` / `find_break`) budgets by display columns rather than bytes.
- **Truncation helpers** — `psi.utf8_text` exposes `safe_head`, `safe_tail`, and `head_chars`. `truncate.truncate_line`, `truncate.bytes` head mode, and the `session_manager` / `slash_commands` preview cuts route through them so a slice never lands inside a multi-byte sequence.
- **JSON surrogate pairs** — `json_pure.decode` now combines `\uD83D\uDE00`-style high+low surrogate pairs into a single astral codepoint and emits 4-byte UTF-8 (was emitting raw CESU-8, which `sanitize_surrogates` later deleted entirely).

## Test plan

- [x] `make lint` (stylua --check, luacheck, cppcheck, gcc -fanalyzer)
- [x] `make check-format-c` (clang-format --Werror)
- [x] `nix run .#infer` — no issues
- [x] `sh tests/build_configs.sh` — full build-config matrix
- [x] `python3 tests/smoke.py --psi build/psi --no-live` — 173 passed, 6 skipped (was 166 before; +7 new UTF-8 cases)
- New smoke tests cover: ASCII / wide / emoji / combining / format cell widths, mixed-width string measurement, multi-byte cursor stepping, backspace deleting whole codepoints, wide-char wrap budgeting in display columns, JSON surrogate-pair decode, codepoint-aligned safe_head / safe_tail.

## Out of scope

Bracketed-paste mode (`\e[?2004h`) and a paste-as-batch event aren't enabled here; with the byte-assembly fix in place, raw pastes of UTF-8 text already flow correctly through the existing path. Adding bracketed paste is a self-contained follow-up.

title: Cache slash-command autocomplete on the TUI hot path
body:
## Summary

Follow-up perf fixes for the slash-command autocomplete added in #63. The current implementation recomputes the full suggestion list (filter + sort + allocate + trim) on every redraw and again on every key event, even when the input has not changed. Each frame walks builtins + aliases, calls `registered_commands()` (sorts), `templates.list()` (sorts), then re-sorts the merged result and copy-trims it.

## What changed

- **`slash_commands`**: generation counter bumped on `register`/`unregister`; memoize both `registered_commands()` and `command_suggestions()` by `(text, limit, registered_version, templates_version)`. Cache the `prompt_templates` module reference (one-time `pcall`). Replace trim-by-copy with in-place `nil` truncation.
- **`prompt_templates`**: bump a version counter in `load()` and cache `list()`. Expose `version()` so callers can detect template changes.
- **`tui_runtime`**: stash the active completion list on state so `layout_rows` and key handling reuse one result. Drop the TUI's `128`-item request to `32` (only 6 rows render). Make `fit_text` count display columns instead of bytes, so multi-byte descriptions truncate at codepoint boundaries and the column padding stays correct.

## Numbers

title: Refactor Forgejo CI workflow to deduplicate jobs
body:
## Summary

The original `.forgejo/workflows/ci.yml` had heavy duplication across 6 jobs: a 7-line manual `git init`/fetch block copy-pasted 6×, identical `HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` setup 6×, near-identical `CI_BUILD_DIR` templates 4×, no concurrency control, and no `needs:` ordering.

### Changes

- **Common env**: introduced `.forgejo/actions/setup`, a local **composite action** that exports `HOME`/`XDG_CACHE_HOME` via `$GITHUB_ENV` and, given a `build-dir-suffix`, also sets `CI_BUILD_DIR` plus the `./build` symlink.
- **Checkout**: stays as a hand-rolled `git init` + token-header block, but hoisted into a workflow-level `FETCH_SCRIPT` env var and `eval`'d in each job. Two reasons we can't use `actions/checkout@v4` here:
  1. The runner image is `nixos/nix:latest` (per `--labels docker:docker://nixos/nix:latest`), which has no Node, and `actions/checkout` is a JS action.
  2. Even if Node were available, the action.yml of any local composite checkout would live in the repo, which isn't on disk yet (chicken-and-egg).
- **Matrix shell**: the inline `bash -euxo pipefail -c '...'` heredoc moved into `scripts/ci/build-and-smoke.sh` so it can be linted and run locally.
- **Concurrency**: `concurrency: { group: ci-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }` so superseded pushes drop the in-flight run.
- **`needs:`**: `infer`, `scan-build`, `valgrind`, `feature-matrix` now wait on `format` + `style`; a lint failure short-circuits expensive runners.
- **Cleanup**: dropped dead `${GITHUB_JOB:-foo}` fallbacks (always set by the runner).

### Why composite still wins (despite the checkout caveat)

Composite actions only need `bash` for `shell: bash` steps — no Node, no Docker — so they run fine in the `nixos/nix:latest` image. They're the right Forgejo-native primitive for the post-checkout setup; only the pre-checkout step is constrained to inline shell.

### Stats

- `ci.yml`: 198 → 134 lines.
- Per-job body: ~17–32 lines → ~5–9 lines.

- [ ] `feature-matrix` variants still receive the right `MAKE_FLAGS` / `SMOKE_EXCLUDES`.
- [ ] Pushing a follow-up commit cancels the in-flight run.

title: MCP review fixes: lazy init, shutdown coverage, redaction, DoS cap
body:
Fixes from a dual-model (Claude+Codex) review of PR #55. Targets feature/mcp-servers so it can land before #55 merges.

## Changes

- **Lazy MCP init.** `psi.tools` no longer fork+initialize MCP servers at module load. Registration is deferred until something actually looks at the tool registry (`find` / `dispatch` / `select_specs` / etc), or the user runs `/mcp` / `/status`. `psi --eval `1+1`` with a slow MCP server in settings goes from 5 s to 33 ms.
- **session-shutdown coverage.** `run_eval`, `run_system_prompt`, `run_compact`, and the REPL slash-command failure path now call `session.announce_shutdown()`, so MCP children shut down cleanly on every mode exit instead of leaking until OS reap.
- **Forgejo auto requires both URL + token.** Defaulting the URL to codeberg.org when only the token was set would have forwarded a self-hosted credential off-host on first boot.
- **`command_label` redaction expanded** from `--token` to a stem denylist (`token`, `api-key`, `apikey`, `key`, `password`, `pass`, `secret`, `auth`, `bearer`, `authorization`, `header`, `access-token`). Covers bare, short, and inline `=VALUE` forms. `/mcp` and `/status` no longer surface argv-borne secrets beyond the original token redaction.
- **`tool_registry.unregister` added.** `register_configured_servers` drops previously-registered MCP tool records before re-registering, so removed servers do not leave closures pointing at a shut-down `Client`.
- **`Client:next_line` capped at 4 MiB** with a protocol error on overflow. A misbehaving (or hostile-via-`mcp-remote`) MCP server can no longer drive psi to OOM with newline-free output.
- **Non-JSON server lines logged to stderr.** Operators can tell server-emits-garbage from a silent timeout.
- **`tools/list` pagination cycle-detected** (track seen cursors, cap at 256 pages).
- **Smoke tests** that read `psi.mcp.status_text` directly now call `tools.ensure_mcp_started()` first, mirroring the interactive path through `/mcp` and `/status`.

## Not addressed

- `psi_process_write` can block the TUI scheduler on a stuck pipe — needs a non-blocking C primitive plus sched-aware Lua loop. Left as a follow-up so this PR stays scoped.

## Verification

- `nix develop -c make` clean (-Werror, -std=c89 -pedantic)
- `nix develop -c tests/smoke.py --psi build/psi --no-live` — 175 passed, 6 skipped
- Manual: `psi --eval `1+1`` with a slow MCP server in settings runs in ~30 ms (was ~5 s); `psi --eval` that explicitly calls `tools.ensure_mcp_started()` still hits the configured timeout.

title: Fix Lua syntax of declarative test headers (level-2 long brackets)
body:
## Why

The `--[[psi-test ... ]]` header introduced in #103 is technically invalid Lua. A level-0 long comment closes at the first `]]` it sees, and our TOML headers contain `[[files]]` etc — Lua treats the inner `]]` as the close. The standalone `lua` interpreter rejects every fixture-bearing test file with `unexpected symbol near ']'`. The tests only run because `lua_runner.py` strips the meta block via regex before `psi --eval` ever sees it.

chroma's Lua lexer follows the same Lua-spec rule, so Forgejo (and GitHub) end multiline-comment highlighting at the inner `]]` and render the rest of the file as garbled Lua. The bug is on our side, not in chroma.

## Fix

Use a level-2 long-bracket comment for the metadata header:

```lua
--[==[psi-test
[[files]]      -- harmless inside a level-2 long comment
]==]
```

- Files are now valid Lua (verified with `lua` 5.2)
- chroma / Forgejo / GitHub highlight the entire header as a comment
- The runner is slightly simpler — the close marker `]==]` is unique, so the line-start lookahead workaround in `_split_meta` is gone

- `tests/lua_runner.py`: `META_OPEN`/`META_CLOSE` -> `--[==[psi-test` / `]==]`; `_split_meta` drops the line-start search


The `docs/portability.md` claim of "no integer-width or endianness assumptions" is verified clean: no byte-order primitives (`htonl`/`bswap`), no shift-assemble of multi-byte ints from byte streams, no integer-over-byte unions, no `*(uint32_t*)buf` punning, no raw-int `fwrite`/`fread`. Embedded blobs are zlib-compressed byte streams, byte-order independent.

Five concrete portability fixes the audit surfaced:

- **`include/psi/abort.h`** — `psi_abort_signal.flag` is written from a SIGINT handler in `cli_mode.c`. C89 only guarantees signal-handler stores via `volatile sig_atomic_t`; the prior `volatile int` rationale rested on per-platform aligned-int atomicity, which the project's stated "no integer-width assumptions" stance disowns.
- **`include/psi/http_tls.h`** — dropped the public `#include <curl/curl.h>` so the header is dep-free. Function now takes `void *curl`; the impl casts back to `CURL *`. Both internal callers already include `curl/curl.h` and pass their `CURL *` directly. Brings `http_tls.h` in line with every other public header (which only pulls `stddef`/`signal`/`stdio`/`lua.h`).
- **`src/runtime/tui_mode.c`** — `setlocale(LC_ALL, "")` was poisoning `LC_NUMERIC`; on a German user's box the JSON encoder would emit `"1,5"` for floats and corrupt provider request bodies. Adopt `LC_CTYPE` only — that's the category TUI text handling actually needs.
- **`scripts/embed.c`** — replaced `%zu` (C99-only conversion specifier) with `%lu` + `(unsigned long)` cast so the host-build tool is C89 conformant on strict toolchains.
- **`src/lua/vm.c`** — `psi.time_ms` registry doc string claimed "monotonic" but the implementation is `gettimeofday` (wall-clock); corrected the description to match the code.

`docs/portability.md` audit table updated with the verified-clean endianness statement and three new green rows.

title: Strip all ill-formed UTF-8 in sanitize_surrogates
body:
## Summary

`prelude.sanitize_surrogates` was a single regex matching the CESU-8 encoding of lone UTF-16 surrogate code points (`ED [A0-BF] [80-BF]`). That covered the original bug — Anthropic returns HTTP 400 *"str is not valid UTF-8: surrogates not allowed"* when those bytes appear in a request body — but the same 400 fires for **any** malformed UTF-8. The error string is misleading.

Real-world reproducer: a gdb session echoing raw bytes via `printf %c` streamed back through the `bash` tool result as stray `0x80-0xBF` continuation bytes. Those leaked past the regex into the on-wire body and tanked the turn.

## Change

Rewrite `sanitize_surrogates` as a proper UTF-8 validator following the Unicode Standard table 3-7:

- Walk the bytes, accept 1/2/3/4-byte sequences with correct lead-byte ranges.
- Range-restrict the second byte for the boundary leads E0/ED/F0/F4 — rejects overlongs, surrogate halves, and code points > U+10FFFF.
- Drop any byte that doesn't start or continue a valid scalar value.

Function name preserved for callsite compatibility (anthropic.lua comments updated to match the broader semantics).

**Performance:** ASCII-only fast path is preserved — if the input contains no high-bit bytes, we return it unmodified. The byte-walker only runs when there's at least one non-ASCII byte.

## Test

`tests/lua/anthropic/sanitize_invalid_utf8.lua` covers:
- valid round-trip (ASCII, 2/3/4-byte sequences, emoji)
- the original CESU-8 lone-surrogate case (regression coverage)
- stray continuation bytes, truncated leads, overlongs
- F4 90 (code point > U+10FFFF)
- the gdb mixed-binary reproducer

## Validation

On `office-desktop` (NixOS, gcc with `-Werror`):

- `make -j8` clean build, no warnings
- `./tests/smoke.py --no-live` → **184 passed, 6 skipped** (live-only)

title: Render edit diffs in unified patch format
body:
Switch the edit tool's diff payload and TUI renderer from psi's custom
numbered format (`<sign><pad-linum> <content>`) to standard **unified
diff format** (`<sign><content>` with `@@` hunk headers and
`--- a/` / `+++ b/` file headers). The output is now a real patch:
copy-pasteable into `patch -p1` or `git apply`.

## Why

The previous format interleaved per-line numbers into the body
(`- 5 line five`), which read nicely but wasn't a valid patch — you
couldn't pipe it into `patch(1)` or `git apply`. Switching to
canonical unified-diff puts those line numbers into the hunk header
(`@@ -1,9 +1,9 @@`) where every diff consumer expects them, and
makes the diff machine-applicable.

## Before / after

`psi edit` of a 9-line file changing `line five` → `LINE FIVE`:

**Before:**

```
  1 line one
  2 line two
  3 line three
  4 line four
- 5 line five
+ 5 LINE FIVE (changed)
  6 line six
  7 line seven
  8 line eight
  9 line nine
    ...
```

**After:**

```
--- a/tmp/diff-demo.txt
+++ b/tmp/diff-demo.txt
@@ -1,9 +1,9 @@
 line one
 line two
 line three
 line four
-line five
+LINE FIVE (changed)
 line six
 line seven
 line eight
 line nine
```

## Trade-offs vs the previous format

* **No per-line numbers in the body.** The hunk header
  `@@ -old_start,old_count +new_start,new_count @@` carries that
  information. Each body line is one byte of sign plus the verbatim
  file content.
* **Distant changes split into multiple hunks** (real unified-diff
  behaviour) instead of being elided with a `...` skip marker. A
  new hunk starts whenever the unchanged gap between two change
  runs exceeds `2 * context_lines` lines.
* **File headers** (`--- a/<path>` / `+++ b/<path>`) are emitted
  when `generate_diff_string` is called with `opts.path`. Absolute
  paths get their leading slash stripped so the `a/` / `b/` prefix
  produces a single slash, matching `git diff`'s convention.
* **Trailing-newline lines** are dropped from the line list when
  both sides have them, so hunk counts match `diff -u` and the
  output round-trips cleanly through `patch -p1`.

## Rendering

The TUI renderer keeps psi's existing palette (red removed, green
added, gray context) and adds:

* **Cyan** for hunk headers (`@@ ... @@`).
* **Bold cyan** for file headers (`--- a/...` / `+++ b/...`).
* Intra-line **inverse** highlight on single-removed + single-added
  pairs is preserved — `-line five` / `+LINE FIVE (changed)` still
  gets the changed substring inverted.

## Tests

* `tests/lua/tool/edit_diff_details`: now checks for `@@` /
  `--- a/` / `+++ b/` and bare `-`/`+` body lines instead of
  numbered prefixes.
* `tests/lua/render/edit_tool_renders_pi_diff_in_call`: checks the
  pre-flight preview surfaces `@@` and bare `-`/`+` lines while
  keeping the success-bg + inverse-highlight assertions.
* `tests/lua/tui/diff_intraline_preserves_utf8`: feeds a real
  unified diff and asserts UTF-8 is preserved.
* `tests/smoke.py`: replaces `diff/generate_numbered_tool_diff` and
  `diff/render_numbered_tool_diff` with unified equivalents
  (`diff/generate_unified_tool_diff`, `diff/render_unified_tool_diff`)
  that additionally assert distant changes split into multiple hunks.

## Verification

* Smoke suite on office desktop: **237 passed, 6 skipped** (same as
  master; the 6 skipped are `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`-gated live tests).
* Round-trip check: generated a multi-edit diff via `preview_edits`,
  wrote it to `/tmp/multi.patch`, applied with `patch -p1 < /tmp/multi.patch`
  — clean apply, no fuzz, both hunks landed.

## Out of scope

Two pi-mono parity gaps remain but aren't part of this PR:

* Word-level intra-line diff (pi uses `Diff.diffWords`; psi still
  uses character-level common-prefix/suffix).
* Fuzzy `oldText` matching (NFKC + smart-quote/em-dash/NBSP
  normalization).

Both are easier follow-ups now that the rendering layer is on
patch format.

Responding to the inline review comments:

- #3300 / #3301: `not not value` is Lua boolean coercion. Since Lua returns operands from `and`/`or` expressions and treats every value except `false`/`nil` as truthy, the double negation normalizes `opts.preserve_whitespace` to the literal booleans `true` or `false` before storing it in `wrap_opts`.

title: Strip symbol tables from nix-packaged static binaries
body:
## Problem

Our nix-packaged binaries ship with their full ELF symbol tables
(`.symtab` + `.strtab`), which on the static musl builds is ~300 KB
of dead weight. The default nix `stripPhase` runs
`strip --strip-debug` on `$out/bin/*`, which removes `.debug_*`
sections but leaves the symbol tables intact. For the cosmocc
derivation we were explicitly running `--strip-debug` ourselves,
which was a no-op (cosmocc already drops `.debug_*` during its own
postprocessing).

## Fix

Two minimal changes, no Makefile / CFLAGS touched:

- `flake.nix` `mkPsi`: add `stripAllList = [ "bin" ]` so nix's
  stripPhase uses `--strip-all` on the binary. Covers `psi`,
  `psi-clang`, `psi-gcc`, `psi-i686`, `psi-static`,
  `psi-static-i686`, `psi-static-riscv64`, `psi-filc`.
- `nix/psi-cosmocc.nix`: switch the explicit strip from
  `--strip-debug` (no-op) to `--strip-unneeded`. `--strip-all` and
  `-Wl,-s` corrupt the APE boot stub ("missing elf symbol table");
  `--strip-unneeded` is the largest safe knob.

`psi-cosmocc-fat` is intentionally left alone — its `stripDebug =
false` is preserved because stripping the fat APE breaks both
embedded ELF dispatch tables (verified: strip drops it from 6.2 MB
to 2.98 MB then it refuses to execute).

## Measurements

Built on office-desktop (`x86_64-linux`), all nix outputs:

| Target | Before | After | Delta |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| psi (dynamic glibc) | 417 808 | 391 280 | −26 KB (−6%) |
| psi-clang | 417 808 | 391 280 | −26 KB (−6%) |
| psi-static (musl) | 3 081 152 | 2 757 696 | −316 KB (−10%) |
| psi-static-i686 | 3 378 160 | 3 071 020 | −300 KB (−9%) |
| psi-cosmocc | 3 525 992 | 3 130 824 | −386 KB (−11%) |
| psi-cosmocc-fat | 6 206 881 | 6 206 881 | unchanged (intentional) |
| psi-tcc | 377 872 | 377 872 | unchanged (already stripped) |
| psi-compcert | 431 672 | 387 272 | −43 KB (−10%) |

## Validation

For each output target, confirmed:

- `psi --version` → `0.1.0`
- `psi --help` → full usage block, exit 0
- `psi --eval 'return _VERSION.." | "..#psi.embedded_doc_names()'`
  → `Lua 5.5 | 7`

Also pulled `psi-static-i686` onto an i686 iSH host (Alpine 3.11,
musl 1.1) and verified the stripped binary still starts and runs
the same lua-side smoke checks.

## Out of scope

Things considered and rejected for this PR:

- `-ffunction-sections -fdata-sections` + `-Wl,--gc-sections`:
  needs Makefile plumbing and per-toolchain opt-out for tcc /
  compcert / cosmocc. Worth doing as a follow-up but a bigger
  surface.
- `-fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-unwind-tables`: could shed
  another ~200–650 KB of `.eh_frame` depending on target, but
  same scope concern.
- `-Wl,-s` link-time strip: breaks cosmocc and fights nix's
  stripPhase; cleaner to let nix do it.

title: perf: efficiency fixes across C core, HTTP, session, TUI, and build
body:
Fixes all findings from a full efficiency audit of the repo. 5 commits, one per subsystem; each was built, tested (313 passed), linted (luacheck 0/0), and format-checked independently.

## Highlights

**C core (`9b7c161`)**
- Buffered HTTP responses grew by exactly one chunk per `realloc` — O(n²) memcpy on large responses. Now geometric with a tracked capacity.
- Shell output spill paid open/write/**fsync**/close per 4 KiB chunk; new `psi.file_append_nosync` used for scratch spill files (session persistence keeps the durable append).
- `psi_process_poll`: `poll(2)` on the pipe instead of 20 ms nanosleep retries, draining up to 64 KiB per call (was one 4 KiB read per Lua round-trip). Abort responsiveness unchanged.

**HTTP (`62436ac`)**
- Process-wide `CURLSH` shares the connection pool + TLS session cache across all easy handles — previously every agent turn paid a fresh TCP+TLS handshake.
- CA bundle (env probe + embedded-bundle zlib inflate) resolved once per process instead of per request. Note: changing `CURL_CA_BUNDLE` mid-process no longer takes effect.
- SSE poll splices the whole chunk queue per call (was one mutex pair + C↔Lua crossing per delta).

**Session/providers (`72ef4d3`)**
- openai_codex accumulated streamed tool-call args by full-string concat *and* re-parsed the entire JSON per delta — doubly quadratic. Now parts-table + parse-once, matching the anthropic/openrouter pattern. Side effect: the finalize malformed-args safety net is now reachable instead of silently dispatching `{}`.
- `sanitize_surrogates`/`decode_utf8_lossy` are span-based; clean strings return the original object with zero allocation. `decode_model_value` is copy-on-write.
- Disk entries built from the live body (no encode→decode round trip); thinking level cached instead of decoding the whole transcript per turn; tool results normalized/encoded once; event-bus handler snapshots cached; file-mutation locks use a FIFO waiter queue instead of a 10 ms sleep-poll.

**TUI (`d62ef46`)**
- Streaming previously cost O(transcript) per provider chunk. Now: 33 ms redraw throttle while busy, suffix-patched flat transcript cache with O(1) totals, and incremental markdown rendering of the live entry (verified byte-identical to full renders across an adversarial corpus of tables/fences/blank-run/wrap cases).
- Input wrapping cached by (input, width, prefixes) — long pasted lines were O(L²) per keystroke.
- tool_call_id→entry index replaces per-chunk reverse scans; C-side render cache compares lines in place instead of strdup-ing every screen line per frame.

**Tools/build (`dce9777`)**
- diff: pure-LF files skip offset mapping entirely (was three per-byte tables per edit); CRLF offsets via sorted CR positions + binary search; common prefix/suffix trimmed before LCS so large files keep real context diffs instead of falling back at `MAX_LCS_CELLS`.
- Bash progress preview recomputed at most every 200 ms (was per 50 ms chunk over a 200 KiB rolling buffer).
- Makefile shell vars snapshotted with `:=`: pkg-config spawns per full build 90 → 12, serial builds ~40% faster; all 16 feature-gate configs verified.
- Shared `lua/psi/base64.lua`; dead `json_pure.lua` removed.

## Deliberately not changed
- Per-write SIGPIPE save/restore in `psi_process_write` — `tests/lua/handles/process_write_sigpipe_scoped.lua` enforces that `os.execute` children inherit default SIGPIPE.
- Per-request `clean_text` re-sanitization kept (system prompts/extension content can bypass append-side sanitization) — now a single allocation-free scan for clean text.
- grep.lua double line-split (bounded at 50 KiB; fusing needs a truncate-module API change) and an mtime cache for auth_storage (no host stat function exists).

title: Route provider notices through the TUI instead of raw stderr
body:
## Summary

Fixes a **visual corruption bug** in the interactive TUI: operational messages such as `psi: auto-compacting ...`, `psi: auto-compaction failed`, auth failures (`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set`, `openai-codex auth failed`), and HTTP/transport errors were written **directly to `io.stderr`** by the providers. Under the alt-screen TUI, a raw stderr write lands in the middle of the rendered frame and scrambles the screen (the "auto compacting failed" / auth lines the user reported showing up out-of-band).

## Fix

Add `psi.notice`, a single sink for out-of-band operational messages:

- `notice.info/warn/error(text)` emit a `"notice"` event via `psi.events` with `{ text, level }`.
- The **TUI subscribes** to `"notice"` and turns each into a proper transcript entry (`info`, or `error` for `warn`/`error`), then redraws — so messages appear in-band and legibly.
- When **no subscriber** is registered (headless CLI), `notice` falls back to `io.stderr:write`, preserving the previous behavior. The presence of the TUI subscriber is what suppresses the raw fallback while the TUI owns the screen.

Converted every direct `io.stderr:write` operational call site to `notice.*`:

| Provider | Sites |
|---|---|
| `anthropic` | auto-compaction progress/failure, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` missing, HTTP post / non-2xx |
| `openai_codex` | auth failure (run_turn + complete_text), completion error |
| `openai_compat` | http post failed, non-2xx, malformed JSON |
| `openrouter` | missing `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` |

## Notes on the reported "compaction failing" symptom

Investigated the live session: `run_compact` itself works correctly (returns a summary and reduces the transcript). The user-visible breakage was the **rendering** of the compaction notices, not compaction logic — which this PR addresses. (In the affected live session, compaction was also re-run successfully out-of-band.)

## Tests

`tests/lua/render/notice_routing.lua` — verifies notices route through the `"notice"` event when a subscriber is present, and fall back (no event) when none is registered.

title: fix(tui): preserve indentation when word-wrapping tool output
body:
## Summary
Fixes the diff/margin bug where diffs and other plain-text tool results rendered left-justified — leading whitespace (indentation) was lost.

## Root cause
The default word-wrapping path (`preserve_whitespace = false`) collapsed every whitespace run to a single space and dropped it at the start of a line. Only the `edit` tool opted into `preserve_whitespace` mode, so `write`/`read` diffs and any indented output lost their leading whitespace. Both the native `psi_vm_text_wrap_ansi` (`src/lua/vm.c`) and the Lua fallback (`lua/psi/tui_text.lua`) had this behavior.

## Fix (pi-aligned)
Aligned with pi's single `wrapTextWithAnsi` algorithm, which preserves whitespace verbatim and only suppresses whitespace that would begin a soft-wrapped continuation line:

- Track the actual whitespace-run width (`pending_space_width`) instead of a collapse-to-one boolean, and emit the full run.
- Preserve a leading whitespace run at the true start of a source line (a line start that is **not** a soft-wrap boundary), tracked via `soft_wrapped`.
- Apply the identical fix to both the native and Lua paths so they stay in parity (`wrap_ansi_lua_fallback_parity` still passes).
- Drop the `edit`-only `preserve_whitespace` special-case in `tool_execution`; all tool output now shares one wrap behavior that keeps indentation.

## Tests
- New: `tests/lua/tui_text/wrap_preserves_indentation.lua` (leading indentation, hard-newline indentation, internal whitespace runs, soft-wrap continuation suppression — for both wrap paths).
- Full suite on office-desktop: **314 passed, 6 skipped**.

title: fix(providers): make provider resolution auth-aware to stop spurious codex OAuth errors
body:
## Summary
Stops spurious `openai-codex` OAuth errors (printed in red) during an Anthropic session. Empty/nil model resolution was falling through to `defaults.provider = openai-codex` even when codex had no credentials, and auto-compaction then retried every turn, spamming "openai-codex auth failed".

## Root cause
`resolve_route` applied implicit fallbacks (`PSI_PROVIDER`, `defaults.provider`, first-known-provider) without checking whether the target provider actually had configured auth. On an Anthropic-only session, background/default resolutions (side-question, compaction) resolved an empty model to codex, which then failed auth.

## Fix (pi-aligned, ports `hasConfiguredAuth`)
- Add `has_auth()` to each provider (anthropic/openrouter/ollama, and openai-codex via a new `oauth_openai_codex.has_credentials()` that checks credential presence without a network refresh).
- Add `api_registry.provider_has_auth(name)`.
- Rewrite `resolve_route` to gate implicit fallbacks on `provider_has_auth`:
  explicit `provider/model` prefix → `PSI_PROVIDER` → `defaults.model` recursion → `defaults.provider` (gated) → `first_authenticated_provider()` over `FALLBACK_PROVIDER_ORDER`, with anthropic as the deterministic hard default.
- Exclude `ollama` from `FALLBACK_PROVIDER_ORDER`: it is a local, credential-less provider whose `has_auth()` is always true, so it would otherwise become the silent default in an unconfigured environment. It remains usable via an explicit `ollama/...` model or `defaults.provider = ollama`.

## Tests
- `tests/lua/providers/resolve_route_auth_gate.lua` covers explicit routing, no-auth default, authed default, no-provider-authed fallback, and the new `ollama_not_implicit=anthropic` case.
- Full suite on office-desktop passes (the two prior `llama3.1`-related failures were caused by the ollama fallback bug fixed here).

body:
## Summary

Brings psi's TUI tab-completion to parity with pi-mono. Previously the completion menu only completed slash-command **names**, was navigated with up/down, and was accepted with **right-arrow** — `Tab` did nothing in the editor. This adds pi's Tab behavior plus argument and file-path completion.

## Behavior (matches pi-mono `editor.ts` / `autocomplete.ts`)

- **Tab accepts** the highlighted completion (right-arrow still works too); when no menu is open, **Tab forces** completion of the current token.
- **Slash-command argument completion**:
  - `/model <Tab>` → model ids (substring match, e.g. `/model claude`)
  - `/theme <Tab>` → registered themes
  - `/thinking <Tab>` → effort levels
  - `/login <Tab>` → providers
  - `/resume`, `/import`, `/export`, `/clone` → filesystem paths
- **File-path completion** for bareword/path-like tokens against the working dir (e.g. `src/ma<Tab>` → `src/main.c`). Directories get a trailing `/` and no auto-space so completion can continue. Path-like tokens (containing `/`, or starting with `.`/`~/`) trigger naturally; bare words only on forced Tab — mirroring pi's split so normal typing isn't noisy.

## Implementation

- New `slash_commands.input_completions(input, cursor, limit, force)` centralizes routing (command-name / command-argument / file-path) and returns `{ start, items }` where each item carries `insert`/`label`/`description`/`trailing`.

body:
## Summary

Brings psi's Up/Down arrow-key behavior into parity with pi-mono's `packages/tui/src/components/editor.ts`.

### Before

psi routed the Up/Down arrows to `tui.transcript.lineUp/lineDown`, which only ever recalled prompt history (or scrolled the transcript) — **regardless of cursor position**. Consequences:

- Pressing **Up** while editing a multi-line draft clobbered the whole buffer with the previous message.
- There was **no way to move the cursor between lines** of a multi-line prompt with the arrows.
- History recall was over-eager: it fired even mid-line.

### After (pi parity)

`chat.editor_arrow_up` / `chat.editor_arrow_down` replicate pi's editor logic:

- **Up**: if not on the first line → move the cursor up one line. On the first line → recall the previous message *only* when the draft is empty, the cursor is at column 0, or we're already browsing history; otherwise jump to line start.
- **Down**: if not on the last line → move the cursor down one line. On the last line → step forward through history if browsing, else jump to line end.
- When there's nothing to move or recall, the arrows **fall through to transcript scroll**, preserving psi's existing affordance. Mouse wheel and PgUp/PgDn are untouched.

Routed from `handle_key_event` ahead of the scroll fallback. Only insert-mode editing with no active selection/search is intercepted, so vim mode, history search, completion menus, and the busy-state queue navigation are unchanged.

Implementation note: the helpers are attached to the existing `chat` table rather than declared as top-level `local`s — `tui_runtime.lua` is at Lua's 200-local-per-main-chunk ceiling and two new top-level locals overflow it.

title: feat(security): gate repo-local resources behind project trust

Ports pi-mono's project-trust model to psi, fixing four findings from `SECURITY-AUDIT.md` (H1, H2, M4, L7).

## What changed

**Project trust (H1, H2, M4).** Repo-local resources — `./.psi/extensions/`, `settings.json`, `keybindings.json`, `prompts/`, `SYSTEM.md`, `APPEND_SYSTEM.md` — now load only when the cwd is trusted. 1. `PSI_TRUST=always|never` env override

4. Global default policy `"project_trust": "ask"|"always"|"never"` in `~/.config/psi/settings.json` (global file only — the gated project file cannot influence the decision)

title: Make Codex bash argument corruption visible and testable
body:
Scope
- Add an OpenAI Codex raw-event regression that streams function-call arguments across hostile SSE chunk boundaries, deliberately withholds the final command character from the deltas, verifies that response.output_item.done is authoritative, dispatches through the real bash/process path, and renders the call/result.
- Render non-whitespace control bytes such as SI (0x0F) as \xNN in bash command previews so invisible corruption is inspectable without changing execution semantics.

Validated diagnosis
- Current psi and current pi-mono both accumulate Responses argument deltas, replace from response.function_call_arguments.done, and finalize from response.output_item.done. No parser truncation was reproduced.
- psi runs bash tool commands through pipes and /bin/sh -lc (cmd.exe /d /c on the supported Windows path), not a PTY. The command bytes are passed as one argv element. A diagnostic such as `sh: prin<SI>: not found` therefore means the shell received `prin` plus SI; it is not evidence that the process layer truncated `print`.
- The regression proves the final `K` in `printf CODEX_OK` survives terminal-event finalization and proves a literal SI byte survives parser, dispatch, shell execution, and captured output. The TUI call preview exposes that SI as `\x0F`.
- The earlier global C0/DEL rejection was removed: arbitrary shell programs can legitimately carry quoted control-byte data, pi-mono does not reject it, and rejecting it would be an unsupported mitigation rather than a fix for the reported source of corruption.

Tests

- `nix develop -c make lint-lua`

title: tui: enforce terminal output ownership
body:
## Summary

Fix TUI warnings and diagnostics clobbering the live input region by making terminal ownership explicit for the full interactive lifetime.

- route runtime diagnostics through a structured, bounded notice queue installed before startup work
- render the frame TUI through one terminal-relative diff owner with synchronized writes
- quarantine accidental stdout/stderr writes to a protected debug log while the TUI owns the terminal
- release and reacquire ownership around suspend and external-editor flows, then re-anchor both frame and chat renderers
- document the ownership contract for extensions and runtime code

## Root cause

The prior fixes covered individual output paths, but startup/runtime warnings could still write directly to raw stderr while the renderer held stale cursor assumptions. A permission warning such as the auth-file mode diagnostic could therefore overlap the current prompt. This change follows pi-mono's central design invariant: one component owns terminal output during interactive rendering, and external owners cross an explicit lifecycle boundary.

## Architecture before this PR

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Startup[Startup and auth checks] -->|raw stderr| Terminal[Terminal]
    Runtime[Runtime callbacks] -->|raw stderr or event| Terminal
    Extensions[Extensions and subprocess glue] -->|stdout and stderr| Terminal
    Events[Late event-based notice handler] --> Renderer[TUI renderer]
    Renderer -->|draw using remembered cursor position| Terminal
    Editor[Editor or suspend lifecycle] -->|temporarily writes outside renderer| Terminal
    Terminal -. out-of-band writes invalidate position .-> Renderer
```

There was no single terminal owner. The renderer remembered where its live region began, but startup diagnostics, extension output, callback errors, and lifecycle transitions could bypass it. Once an out-of-band write moved the hardware cursor, the renderer's logical position no longer described the real terminal. Its next redraw could then overwrite or overlap the prompt.

Notice routing was also coupled to event-handler presence and installed too late to cover all startup work. Fixing one warning call site therefore could not establish a general invariant: another direct write, reload, callback, or suspend/editor transition could recreate the same class of corruption.

## Architecture after this PR

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Diagnostics[Startup and runtime diagnostics] --> Notice[psi.notice structured sink]
    Notice --> Queue[Bounded and coalesced notice queue]
    Queue --> Renderer[Single TUI render owner]
    Renderer --> Writer[psi.tui_write]
    Writer --> PrivateFD[Private terminal file descriptor]
    PrivateFD --> Terminal[Terminal]

    Stray[Accidental stdout, stderr, or psi.log] --> Guard[Whole-life stdio guard]
    Guard --> DebugLog[Protected 0600 debug log]

    External[External editor or suspend] --> Release[Restore stdio and terminal mode]
    Release --> ExternalOwner[External process owns terminal]
    ExternalOwner --> Reclaim[Reclaim guard and raw mode]
    Reclaim --> Reanchor[Forget stale region and re-anchor]
    Reanchor --> Renderer
```

During interactive operation, only the renderer writes to the visible terminal, through a private descriptor that is not inherited by children. Structured diagnostics enter a bounded queue instead of drawing synchronously. The runtime drains that queue only at a safe render boundary, after any mutable streaming suffix is closed, so bursts of warnings cannot interleave with prompt or assistant rendering.

The stdio guard is deliberate failure containment. Code that still writes directly to stdout or stderr cannot corrupt the UI; its output is redirected to a nonblocking, no-follow, mode-`0600` debug log, with `/dev/null` as a fail-closed fallback. Expected user-visible diagnostics must use `psi.notice`.

Suspend and external-editor operations are explicit ownership transfers. Psi restores stdio and terminal state before handing control away. On return it reacquires the guard and raw mode, discards any stale frame/chat cursor accounting, anchors at the terminal's current cursor, and performs a fresh render. Failed release or reacquisition is fatal rather than allowing two components to believe they own the terminal.

This is parity with pi-mono at the architectural level: one retained UI owns terminal output, diagnostics are structured inputs to that UI, captured subprocess output is not allowed to draw arbitrarily, and external terminal owners cross explicit stop/restart boundaries.

## Verification

- `make -j2 build/psi`
- `make BUILD_DIR=build-ci-style lint` (the exact CI style/static-analysis target, including GCC `-fanalyzer`)
- `make check-format-c`
- `make analyze-cppcheck`
- `make check-build-configs`
- generated documentation idempotence check
- `python3 tests/smoke.py --psi build/psi --no-live` — 407 passed, 6 skipped
- independent correctness and efficiency audits found no remaining blockers
- Forgejo CI — all 21 jobs passed on amended head `a0c3c69`

Focused PTY coverage includes auth warnings in frame/chat modes, extension stdout/stderr quarantine, `/reload`, external editor, suspend/resume, relative renderer behavior, and bounded notice routing.

The first CI run identified GCC analyzer's inability to model the intentional cross-function lifetime of the `dup2`-redirected standard descriptors. The amended head applies the same narrow analyzer suppression already used by the subprocess redirection path; the exact failing CI target and replacement workflow pass.

title: docs: seed a gallery showing psi on Tiny Core Linux
body:
Seeds `docs/gallery.md` + `images/` with a first entry: psi running on **TinyCorePure64 16.2 (x86_64)**.

The premise of the gallery is minimality — each entry is about what the host *doesn't* have. This one has no compiler, no `git`, no `python`, no `file`, no `readelf`, no `ldd`. psi is a single **2.8 MB statically linked binary** dropped into `/opt/psi`; nothing else was installed to make it run.

### Captures

| | |
|---|---|
| `01-tinycore-desktop` | Stock flwm/wbar desktop, Xfbdev on vesafb |
| `02-uname-and-binary-size` | `2,823,456` bytes — the whole install |
| `03-agent-identifies-system` | psi shells out to `uname`/`os-release`/`lscpu`, and infers from the `hypervisor` flag + `AMD-V` line that it's a guest, not bare metal |
| `04-agent-writes-and-runs-script` | Full write → chmod → exec → verify loop with no dev tooling present |
| `05-agent-parses-elf-by-hand` | The best one — see below |

The ELF capture is the one worth looking at. Asked whether its own binary is static, psi reaches for `file`, `readelf` and `ldd`; none exist here, and `ldd` segfaults (the classic symptom on a static binary). So it parses the ELF header directly with `od`, walks the eight program headers, and concludes from the absence of `PT_INTERP` and `PT_DYNAMIC` that no runtime loader is involved.

### Also included

`tinycore/` — the scripts that reproduce the VM:

- `build.sh` bakes psi, credentials and a `bootlocal.sh` hook into the TinyCore initrd as an appended cpio
- `provision-disk.sh` one-shot headless boot that partitions/formats the persistent disk
- `run-vm.sh` boots it with the desktop on VNC
- `guest-run.sh` / `guest-type.py` drive the guest from the host over a serial control channel and the QEMU monitor

Two findings baked into those scripts as comments, since both cost real debugging time:

- **`/opt` must not be persisted.** With `opt=sda1` the first boot's copy of psi and `bootlocal.sh` wins forever and later rebuilds silently stop taking effect.
- **`vga=` is mandatory.** TinyCorePure64 runs Xfbdev on vesafb, and the kernel's only framebuffer driver is vesafb — no bochs-drm, qxl or virtio-gpu. Without a `vga=` mode set by the real-mode boot code there is no `/dev/fb0` and X dies at startup, leaving a stale `/tmp/.X11-unix/X0` that then blocks restart.

### Notes

- Credentials (`overlay/auth.json`, `env.sh`, `vncpasswd`) and all build artifacts are gitignored; only the scripts are tracked. Staged content was scanned for key material before commit.
- The screenshots use psi's CLI mode rather than the TUI. The TUI's box-drawing characters (`U+2500`) don't render in this guest — aterm isn't UTF-8 capable, and neither lxterminal/VTE nor urxvt resolved the glyph even with DejaVu installed and `fc-match` confirming it. Worth chasing separately if TUI screenshots are wanted; it doesn't affect psi itself.

title: tui: detect terminal charset and fall back to ASCII glyphs
body:
psi probed `TERM` to decide whether ANSI escapes were safe, then emitted Unicode **unconditionally**. Those are independent capabilities: a terminal can honour CSI sequences perfectly while running under a non-UTF-8 locale, where multi-byte glyphs arrive as mojibake or missing-glyph boxes.

### The case that surfaced it

Tiny Core Linux: `TERM=xterm-256color` with `LANG=C`, and `locale -a` offering only `C` and `POSIX` — no UTF-8 locale exists on the system at all. psi's existing check passes on `TERM`, so colour renders correctly, while every box-drawing character, the braille spinner and the bullets come out as tofu.

Confirmed this is not a font problem: it reproduces with DejaVu installed and `fc-match "DejaVu Sans Mono"` resolving correctly, across both VTE and rxvt.

### Changes

**`platform.unicode_supported()`** reads the charset from the locale with POSIX precedence (`LC_ALL`, then `LC_CTYPE`, then `LANG`), plus a `PSI_UNICODE` override for terminals whose *font* lacks the glyphs even though the charset is fine. Windows isn't described by these variables, so it keeps its current behaviour.

**`psi.glyphs`** follows the `psi.ansi` convention — callers read `glyphs.bullet` / `glyphs.hrule` and get an ASCII stand-in when the charset can't carry the preferred form, rather than branching themselves. Deliberately separate from `psi.ansi`, since a single "fancy output" flag would get exactly this case wrong.

### Scope

Two commits, because the first pass was incomplete and a table in the guest caught it:

1. Detection + `psi.glyphs`, wired through the TUI chrome (borders, spinner, prompt caret, radio buttons, tool-result corners) and `psi.markdown`. Markdown is included because it renders **CLI** output too — the bullet and blockquote bar were tofu there as well, not just in the TUI.
2. Tables and the remaining chrome. Tables draw their own borders in `psi.tui_components.markdown` rather than going through `psi.markdown`, so they needed the fallback separately. Also the em dashes that reach a terminal: provider error hints, the `/export` transcript header, auth picker labels, the provider doc table. The ones in `psi.prompt` are left alone — they go into the system prompt, not to a terminal.

ASCII forms are all one column wide, like the box drawing they replace, so column arithmetic is unaffected:

```
+------+-------+
| lang | size  |
+------+-------+
| C    | 2.8MB |
+------+-------+
```

### Verification

- 348 lua cases pass; `make lint-lua` clean.
- 6 new tests covering UTF-8 vs C locale, `LC_ALL` precedence over `LC_CTYPE`/`LANG`, the `PSI_UNICODE` override, markdown bullet/blockquote fallback, and ASCII table borders.
- Verified end-to-end on the actual Tiny Core guest, not just synthetically: the TUI renders `|` spinner, `-` rules, `>` prompt and `*` separators with no tofu, and `render_table` emits pure ASCII under `LANG=C`.

Stacked conceptually on #205 (the gallery), but independent — this branch is off `master` and touches no `tinycore/` files.
