## Problem

Observed live: an agent's bash tool ran `git push` against an http remote with no credentials; git sat on an interactive `Username for ...:` prompt (git reads `/dev/tty` directly). When the git child died, psi never noticed — the spinner kept rendering, and Ctrl-C did not unwind the turn; psi had to be SIGKILLed.

Root cause: a tool child can outlive its output stream (daemonizing child, or one blocked on `/dev/tty`), producing pipe EOF while the child is still alive. `psi_process_poll` correctly reports done in that situation (a12e6a8 reaps dead children even when a grandchild holds the pipe open), but `psi_process_finish` then sat in an uninterruptible `waitpid(pid, ..., 0)` that never checked the abort signal. The worker thread blocked forever while the main thread kept rendering, and the abort flag had nobody left to notice it.

## Fix (pi-mono parity)

- Dead child → tool call returns with the exit status surfaced (existing poll-side reap, now covered end-to-end).
- Abort → the turn unwinds promptly: `psi_process_finish` now waits with `WNOHANG` at poll granularity, watching the abort signal; on abort it SIGTERMs the process group, escalates to SIGKILL after 500ms, and caps the wait at ~1.5s (POSIX and cosmopolitan/Windows paths).
- `finish()` now always closes its pipe/stdin fds; previously they leaked whenever `poll()` had already reaped the child.

## Tests

- `handles/process_finish_eof_child_alive`: EOF with a live child still returns the real exit status.
- `handles/process_finish_abort_unwinds`: abort during finish unwinds with status 130 instead of hanging (hangs ~60s pre-fix; verified the test wedges against the old binary).
- `tool/bash_child_outlives_pipe`: bash tool surfaces `Command exited with code 3` instead of wedging the turn.

Full suite: 345 passed.

title: Whitelist CVE-2026-67215 as not applicable to psi
body:
## Problem

The `SBOM audit` CI job (severity ≥ 7 gate) has been failing on every PR since the late-July NVD ingest of the cJSON CVE batch — this is what was red on PR #206 and #208, not their code.

[CVE-2026-67215](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-67215) (CVSS 7.5): uncontrolled recursion → stack exhaustion in `cJSONUtils_ApplyPatches()` / `cJSONUtils_ApplyPatchesCaseSensitive()` — the RFC 6902 JSON Patch helpers. A crafted patch document amplifies document depth past what `cJSON_Delete()` can unwind.

## Why psi is not affected

- The vulnerable code lives in `cJSON_Utils.c` (RFC 6902 patching), not the core parser.
- psi links only **`-lcjson`** (never `-lcjson_utils`) — see `PSI_LIBS_CJSON` in `flake.nix`.
- `grep -r cJSONUtils\|ApplyPatches` across `src/`, `include/`, `lua/` is empty: no JSON Patch application path exists.
- psi's parser exposure goes through `cJSON_Parse` with `CJSON_NESTING_LIMIT` (1000), which the CVE explicitly does not bypass (the recursion is in patch-driven `cJSON_Duplicate`/`cJSON_Delete`).

## Validation

`nix run .#audit-sbom -- .#default sbom` with this entry on office-desktop: `runtime vulnerability threshold passed: no unwhitelisted findings >= 7`.

If upstream cJSON ships a fixed release, the better long-term fix is advancing the pin; until then this documents the non-applicability.

title: Respect short terminal and prompt viewports
body:
## Summary

- stop promoting terminals shorter than 12 rows to a synthetic 12-row inline frame
- size the prompt viewport like pi-mono: `max(5, floor(terminalRows * 0.3))`
- cap that target to physically available rows in frame mode while allowing chat mode to scroll its five-row minimum naturally
- crop unavoidable tiny-frame chrome around the actual editor cursor marker, keeping emitted height and hardware cursor coordinates inside the physical viewport

Before this change a 4-row terminal rendered a 12-row frame, and a 24-row prompt could consume 18 rows. It now renders exactly 4 rows, while the standard prompt viewport is 7 rows. title: fix(tui): align Lua fallback cell wrapping
body:
## Reproduction

With all terminal text host primitives, including `psi.cell_width`, disabled before loading `psi.tui_text`:

- `بّ` measured 2 cells instead of the native/pi-compatible 1, so wrapping `AبّB` at width 2 split the combining shadda away from its base.
- U+303F IDEOGRAPHIC HALF FILL SPACE measured 2 cells instead of 1, moving clip/wrap boundaries one column early.
- with only native wrapping disabled, `{ preserve_whitespace = true }` did not track OSC 8 state, so a hyperlink spanning a wrap was neither closed on the first line nor reopened on the continuation.

## Fix

- add the Unicode 17 pre-Indic zero-width combining ranges used by the C host to the dependency-free Lua width fallback
- preserve the classic U+303F narrow-width exception
- route preserve-whitespace escape handling through the existing SGR+OSC state tracker
- add fully host-disabled width/index/clip/wrap parity coverage and BEL/ST OSC 8 native/fallback comparisons

This is intentionally independent of #220: it does not duplicate Indic linker/consonant tables. #220 owns Indic conjunct segmentation; this PR owns earlier-script combining marks and generic fallback ANSI/cell behavior.

## Validation

- `make -j2 build/psi`
- focused fallback parity tests (2 passed)
- `pytest -q tests/test_lua_cases.py --psi ./build/psi` (354 passed)
- `python3 tests/smoke.py --psi ./build/psi --no-live`
